prompt:
Implement configurable line-number labels throughout Pygments' HTML, SVG, RTF, terminal and groff output. Applications should be able to label displayed line numbers, for example L[0001], without changing source text or post-processing a highlighted document. Complete this as a maintained public feature across the formatter implementations, tests, CLI examples and documentation.

Public API: Formatter accepts lineno_prefix and lineno_suffix string options, both defaulting to the empty string, and exposes their validated values as instance attributes. Each supplied value must be a string containing no carriage return or newline; otherwise raise pygments.util.OptionError naming the option during formatter construction, even if line numbers are disabled. Empty strings and Unicode text are valid. Preserve all other option defaults, supported Python versions and formatter discovery. The same options work through ordinary formatter constructors, get_formatter_by_name, highlight/format and pygmentize -O/-P.

Implement actual rendering in HtmlFormatter's table and inline line numbers, SvgFormatter, RtfFormatter, TerminalFormatter, Terminal256Formatter, TerminalTrueColorFormatter and GroffFormatter. Affixes surround the complete existing numeric field, including that formatter's existing numeric padding: a terminal's 0001 becomes PREFIX0001SUFFIX and retains its existing ': ' separator; HTML/RTF/groff keep their native numeric padding inside the affixes. The label belongs to the existing line-number element/group and retains its styles. Preserve the existing visible-number selection, linenostart, linenostep and linenospecial behavior wherever supported, and preserve the existing handling of trailing newlines, empty input and final partial lines. A suppressed number is a blank field reserving the full label width, including both affixes, without displaying either affix. No labels appear when line numbering is disabled. Do not add line numbers to source tokens.

Affixes are plain text, escaped for their destination format. HTML and SVG labels must survive characters such as <, &, quotes and Unicode as text without injecting elements or changing links. RTF labels must escape braces and backslashes and encode Unicode with valid RTF text escapes. Groff labels must escape request/control characters, backslashes and Unicode using the formatter's text conventions. Terminal labels retain Unicode text and use ordinary line-number styling. Do not rewrite the source token values, global styles or shared formatter registries. HTML line anchor IDs, numeric href targets and highlighted-line selection stay numeric and unchanged; the label changes visible text only. Full documents, inline styles, encoded output and style definitions continue to work.

Preserve layout. HTML/RTF blank number fields reserve the same character width as a visible label. Groff wrapped continuation lines include the extra prefix and suffix width in their number-column indentation; wrapping of source content itself stays as before. SVG continues to honor the caller's linenowidth and existing source coordinates. Reusing one of these formatter instances for a second document must start that document's line numbering and wrap accounting independently, with the same output as a fresh instance configured identically. Interleaving separate instances with different labels must remain isolated. Token input may be a one-shot generator with fragmented tokens and blank lines; keep the existing buffering behavior and do not require a re-iterable token source.

Add focused regressions in the relevant existing HTML, HTML line-number, RTF, terminal, groff and formatter test modules, plus SVG/integration coverage. Cover default compatibility, disabled numbering, escaping, Unicode, numeric padding, skipped numbers, anchors, encoded output, repeated instances, fragmented streams and wrapping. Document both public options and affected formatter behavior, with runnable Python and command-line examples. Run the full repository test suite and its available source/style checks, addressing regressions introduced by the feature. Finish with a concise implementation and verification report. Make routine implementation choices autonomously.
